primary_question: Which environmental gradients are associated with each biological capitulum trait, and how are these traits integrated into a capitulum?
framing_revision: User-directed clarification after results were available; not a new preregistration and not a change to numerical tests or multiplicity families
primary_questions: Trait-specific environmental associations followed by sampling, spatial and among-taxon placement sensitivity
Within-module versus between-module phenotypic integration and its correspondence across scales
workflow: Reuse measured continuous traits and PR93 biological definitions
Retain complete marginal environment atlas and original multiplicity families
Apply inherited sampling, spatial and among-taxon phylogenetic placement sensitivity
Integrate response patterns with existing whole-capitulum trait organization
surface_traits: supporting measurement analyses, not equal-status biological constructs
within_among: retain distinct estimands internally and in labelled results; environment-first presentation does not pool scales
environment: same nine gradients as PR93; marginal, not mutually adjusted effects
whole_capitulum: Use all nine constructs, not just environment-significant traits, to examine phenotypic organization. Module-label permutations and cross-scale matrix alignment address this question; neither reconstructs evolutionary change
bridge: Existing exploratory comparison of phenotypic integration with environmental-profile similarity; retain unsupported coupling
omnibus_environment: supplementary separate question; retain all 18 unsupported tests, not a prerequisite or test of integration, independence or evolutionary modularity
adaptation_boundary: Robust environmental associations motivate functional/adaptive hypotheses, but do not establish adaptation, selection or independence from all phylogenetic history
no_changes: No automatic promotion of v2 anchor associations
No merging PR92 PR93 or main
first_execution: reproducible synthesis of existing PR93 numerical artifacts, not a new independent reanalysis
